messages.text:
## What was wrong

The sign-in redirect built its OAuth `state` without the workspace id, so the callback had nothing to return to and sent everyone to their **default workspace**.

## The fix

- `state.ts` now signs the workspace id into the state
- `callback.ts` checks access and redirects back
- a stale id falls back to the picker instead of a 404

```ts
export function buildState(workspaceId: string) {
  // signed so the callback can trust it
  return sign({ workspaceId, nonce: randomUUID() }, 600)
}
```

| Suite | Passed | Failed | Time |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| auth | 12 | 0 | 1.4s |
| workspace | 7 | 0 | 0.9s |
| redirect | 4 | 0 | 0.3s |

All 23 tests pass. The [OAuth state rules](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-10.12) are why the id is signed rather than passed in the query.
